title: Noise stability and sublinear total influence
statement: For every natural number $k$, the class of Boolean functions admitting a polynomial threshold representation of Fourier degree at most $k$ is uniformly noise stable if and only if it has uniformly sublinear total influence. Here uniform noise stability means there is a function assigning a probability in $[0,1]$ to each noise parameter in $[0,1/2]$, tending to zero as the parameter tends to zero through positive values, that bounds the noise sensitivity of every function in the class at every such parameter. Uniformly sublinear total influence means there is a sequence of probabilities in $[0,1]$ tending to zero that bounds, for every dimension $n$, the total influence of each function in the class by $n$ times the corresponding probability.
hypotheses_covered: Noise-stability bound holds for every dimension, every function in the class, and every parameter in [0, 1/2]
Noise-stability modulus takes values in [0, 1] and tends to zero as the parameter tends to zero through positive values
Total-influence bound holds for every dimension and every function in the class
Influence modulus takes values in [0, 1] and tends to zero as the dimension tends to infinity
